user_input: It's DSA coding lab selection day and everyone immediately paired up within like five seconds. I just sat there staring at my IDE, pretending to write a header file while my heart was hammering against my ribs, terrified someone would notice I was the only one left without a partner. I ended up getting assigned to a random group of three who didn't even look at me when I sat down, and now I'm back in my hostel room having skipped dinner because the thought of walking into the mess hall alone and finding a table makes me want to throw up. I'm paying lakhs in fees just to feel like a completely invisible ghost who can't even write a line of code or make a single friend.

Tomorrow is the placement drive orientation and we have to do these 30-second elevator pitches in front of the entire batch. My hands are literally shaking while typing this because my CGPA is already low and my public speaking is absolute trash. Everyone in the hostel corridor is talking about their resumes and mock interviews, and I'm just locked in my room, staring at the ceiling, feeling like a massive fraud who is going to freeze up and get laughed off the stage. I feel so incredibly alone in this; it's like everyone got the manual on how to be a normal, functioning adult and I missed the distribution.

My roommate's birthday was yesterday and the room was packed with people laughing, sharing inside jokes, and eating cake. I was sitting right there on my lower berth, staring at my phone pretending to be super busy debugging a backlog project, but my throat was so tight I could barely swallow. Nobody even offered me a piece of cake or asked if I wanted to join the photo, and I felt this paralyzing fear that if I spoke up or tried to squeeze into the frame, they'd all just stare at me like 'who invited this guy?' I ended up going to the common washroom and crying quietly in the toilet stall just to escape the suffocating feeling of being lonely in a crowded room.

I've been skipping the mess during peak hours and only going down at 10 PM right before it closes, just to avoid the corridor walks where everyone is walking in groups of five or six laughing. Whenever I hear steps behind me in the hostel corridor, my heart starts racing and I pull out my phone pretending to look at urgent WhatsApp notifications so I don't have to make awkward eye contact. I feel like a complete freak because I want to talk to people so badly, but the moment someone actually says 'hi' in the lift, my brain short-circuits, my face gets hot, and I just give a weird nod and walk away fast. I'm sabotaging my own chances of making friends and now I'm just completely stuck in this empty room.

I joined the coding club thinking it would help me find my crowd, but at the first meeting, everyone was already talking about their winter internships and cracking jokes in their regional language. I sat at the very back row, sweating through my hoodie, trying to look interested in the slides but secretly counting down the minutes until I could leave without drawing attention to myself. I haven't gone back since, and now I see their WhatsApp group flooding with photos of their weekend trips and outings. I feel this massive, crushing guilt that I'm wasting my college years being a coward while everyone else is living their best life and building networks.

I dread going to the mess hall for dinner. Everyone sits in these loud, laughing groups of eight, and I just stand there with my plate, my hands literally shaking, looking for any empty spot where I won't be in anyone's way. Yesterday, I tried to sit with a few guys from my lab, but as soon as I sat down, the conversation just died and they started texting on their phones. I choked down my food in five minutes and ran back to my room; I'd rather eat dry Maggi alone in my dark hostel room than face that suffocating silence again.

For the DBMS term project, the professor said 'form groups of three' and my heart just dropped to my stomach. Within two seconds, everyone was screaming, high-fiving, and locking in their partners while I just sat there staring at my blank screen, pretending to edit my GitHub profile so no one would see how humiliated I was. No one looked at me, no one asked. I'm literally going to end up in the 'leftover' pool assigned by the TA, and the thought of working with people who are forced to have me in their team makes me want to drop the course entirely.

I queued up for hours for the coding club recruitment interview, but when I walked into the room and saw five seniors sitting there staring at me, my throat completely locked up. I couldn't even explain a basic bubble sort, something I've coded a hundred times, and my voice was trembling so hard they had to offer me water. I saw one of them write something down and smirk, and I just know they're going to joke about the anxious kid who couldn't even speak in the hostel common room later. I hate myself for being this weak.

I'm staring at the wing's WhatsApp group and everyone is planning a trip to the local hills this weekend, splitting cab fares, and sharing memes. I'm right here in the same corridor, my door is literally open, but nobody knocked or asked if I wanted to join. I feel like this invisible ghost walking through the hostel corridors, where everyone knows my face but no one actually wants me there. I want to mute the group but I'm terrified that if I do, I'll miss the one time someone actually remembers I exist.

I haven't even cleared a single coding round because my hands sweat so much during proctored tests that I keep making stupid syntax errors. Yesterday, I heard some batchmates in the balcony laughing about how 'some guys don't even know how to write a basic API' and I just shrank back into my bed, pulling the covers over my head. I'm so terrified of failing my parents and becoming the local joke of this batch.

I can hear the mess hall noise from my window—the plates clashing, people laughing, shouting across tables—and my stomach literally knots up. I feel like a total freak sitting here in the dark while everyone else is making core memories and finding their groups.

No one looked my way, and now I'm the only one left without a partner, probably going to get assigned randomly to some leftover group. Everyone is talking about the Day-1 placement drives, and I'm losing my mind. I was standing in the corridor outside the seminar hall, and my hands were shaking so bad I couldn't even hold my resume folder straight. Every time someone walked past, I felt like they were judging my CGPA or my awkward posture. I couldn't breathe, so I hid in the disabled toilet stall for forty minutes until the crowd cleared out. I want to make friends and talk to people, but my chest feels like it's being squeezed by a metal band whenever I try to speak.

I dread the dinner mess hours more than my backlogs. Everyone sits in these tight-knit circles, speaking their regional languages and laughing at inside jokes, while I just sit at the corner table staring at my plate. I keep my phone open, pretending to read some documentation, but my hands are literally trembling. If someone even accidentally makes eye contact, I panic and look away. I’m so lonely my chest literally aches, but the thought of carrying my plate over to someone's table makes me feel like I’m going to throw up.

I forced myself to go to the cultural club orientation today because my roommate said I need to 'get out more.' But as soon as the room filled up, I froze. I tried to introduce myself to this girl sitting next to me, but my voice cracked, and she just gave this polite, pitying smile before turning back to her friends. I spent the rest of the time looking at the floor, feeling this burning shame in my face. I came back to my room, locked the door, and I've been staring at the wall for hours—I hate how impossible it is for me to just exist normally around people.

My hostel wing is empty this weekend because of the long break. I heard the guys next door planning a trip to some hill station, laughing and packing their bags. I wanted so badly to step out and ask if I could join, but I was literally paralyzed behind my closed door, terrified they’d think I’m some desperate loser clinging onto them. Now they're gone, the corridor is completely silent, and the silence is just pounding in my ears. I’m trapped between being terrified of people and being absolutely broken by this isolation.

It's been a month since the semester started and I still can't bring myself to sit next to anyone in the DSA lab. Today the professor asked us to pair up for a graph traversal problem and my chest literally tightened up; I just stared at my screen pretending to debug an already compiled code until everyone had partners. I ended up doing the lab alone, and now I'm back in my hostel room skipping dinner because the thought of walking into the mess hall and looking for a seat makes me want to throw up.

We have mock placement presentations in English next week and my hands are literally shaking just typing this. I have this horrible stutter that only comes out when everyone is looking at me, and I know the guys in the back row are going to snicker and mock my accent like they did during the orientation day. I'd rather take a zero or get a backlog in this module than stand at the podium and let fifty people watch me crumble.

There’s a birthday celebration happening in the hostel corridor right now for one of the guys in my wing, and I can hear them laughing and slamming doors through my wall. I stayed in my room with the lights off because I didn't want to awkwardly stand on the edge of the circle pretending to be part of the group when I barely know how to make small talk. My phone is completely silent, and I'm just sitting here in the dark wondering if I'm going to spend all four years of this degree being the invisible guy who couldn't even say happy birthday.

I tried going to the mess hall today during the lunch rush, but every single table was packed with groups speaking their native regional languages and laughing so easily. I stood there holding my plate for what felt like an eternity, feeling everyone's eyes on my awkward posture, before I panicked, dumped my untouched food in the bin, and ran back to my room. I hate my social anxiety so much; it makes me feel like an alien who doesn't even deserve a basic meal.

I forced myself to go to the web development club recruitment meet today because my senior told me it's good for placements. But when it was my turn to introduce myself and talk about my tech stack, my throat completely locked up and I just muttered 'nothing yet' and sat down, even though I've been learning React for six months. I saw two guys in the front row exchange a look and smile, and I've been crying in the common washroom stall for the last twenty minutes because I ruined my only chance to network.

Everyone in my hostel wing is going out to the tea stall near the gate, and I can hear them laughing through my closed door. I tried opening my door twice to join, but my chest got so tight I couldn't breathe, so I just locked it and sat on the floor. I'm literally failing my DSA coding labs because I'm too terrified to ask the TA for help, and now I'm just rotting in my room while everyone else is building a life.

It’s third year and the placement cell just released the mock group discussion schedules. I saw the list of names in my batch and my stomach just turned to water. I know I’m going to freeze up and look like an idiot in front of the placement coordinators and my peers who already have high-paying summer internships. I can't even speak in a 5-person hostel mess conversation without my voice shaking, how am I supposed to survive a GD?

I forced myself to go to the college cultural fest orientation today because my parents keep asking if I'm making friends or just wasting my CGPA. I sat in the third row, but as the room started filling up and people were high-fiving and sitting together, I felt like there was a giant spotlight on me showing everyone how friendless I am. I pretended to get an urgent call, walked out, and now I'm hiding in the library washroom crying my eyes out.

We have to form groups of four for our final year capstone project by Friday or the HOD will randomly assign us. Everyone is WhatsApping each other and locking their teams, and I’m just staring at my phone waiting for someone, anyone, to ask me, but my chat list is dead. I want to message my lab partner but my hands freeze up thinking about the humiliation of them saying they're already full.

It’s my birthday today and my phone has been completely silent except for a text from my mom and a template email from the library. I walked past the common room earlier and saw my batchmates celebrating someone else's birthday with cake and music, and I felt this physical ache in my chest like I’m totally invisible. I want to go down to the mess for dinner because I'm starving, but the thought of sitting at a long table alone while everyone looks at me makes me want to jump out of my skin.

Every time the prof says 'form groups of four for the DBMS project', my stomach literally drops. I just sit there staring at my VS Code screen, pretending I'm super busy debugging some stupid loop, hoping someone will randomly ask me to join. Everyone else is high-fiving, talking about their weekend plans, and I'm just this invisible ghost who got a 9.2 CGPA but can't even look another human in the eye without shivering. I ended up doing the last lab solo and lost 10% marks because 'collaboration is mandatory.' I'm so lonely it physically hurts, but the thought of asking someone to group up makes me want to throw up.

I've been in this hostel for a month now and I still can't go to the mess without my earphones blasted at max volume. Yesterday, some guys from the senior wing sat near me and started talking about placements and DSA prep, and I literally choked on my rotis because I was so terrified they'd ask me my name or branch. I ended up leaving half my plate and running back to my room. Everyone seems to have found their 'gang' already, laughing at inside jokes, while I'm eating instant noodles at 2 AM just to avoid walking down that corridor.

Mock interviews started today and I completely froze during the HR round. The interviewer asked me a simple question about my hobbies and my mind went entirely blank, my hands started shaking, and I couldn't breathe. I have a solid GitHub profile and cracked three LeetCode hard problems yesterday, but none of that matters if I can't talk to a human interviewer without looking like a trembling mess. I see my batchmates chatting up recruiters on LinkedIn so easily, and I'm just here thinking I'm going to end up unplaced and alone because of my broken brain.

I forced myself to go to the coding club's orientation today because my roommate said it would help with networking. But as soon as I entered the seminar hall and saw eighty people chatting, laughing, and throwing paper planes, my chest tightened up so badly. I stood near the door for two minutes, pretending to look at a text on my phone, and then I just turned around and bolted back to the library. I spent the next three hours crying in the washroom because I'm so sick of being the guy who can't even sit in a room with his peers without having a mini-stroke.

Everyone in our wing is in this unofficial WhatsApp group where they plan weekend trips, late-night tea runs, and valorant matches. I'm in the group too, but I never send a single text because I spend forty minutes draft-deleting a simple 'hey, can I join?' thinking they'll find me annoying or just ignore me. Last night I watched them all walk past my door laughing, heading out for a birthday treat, and my room felt like a concrete coffin. I'm literally paying to live in a hostel full of people, yet I've never felt more agonizingly alone.

We had to form groups of four for the DBMS project today, and my heart was literally hammering against my ribs. Everyone immediately turned to their friends, laughing and high-fiving, while I just stared at my laptop screen pretending to debug a broken SQL query so I wouldn't look pathetic. I ended up being the last person left, and the prof had to manually assign me to a random group that clearly didn't want me. I've been hiding in my hostel room since 4 PM, skipping dinner because the thought of walking into that crowded mess hall and having no one to sit with makes me want to throw up.

I can't even stand up in the DSA lab to ask the TA a basic doubt because I'm terrified the guys next to me will laugh or think I'm stupid for not getting it. During the mock placement interviews yesterday, my voice literally shook and my mind went completely blank on a simple array reversal question I've done ten times. Everyone else is cracking off-campus referrals, chatting up seniors, and making networks on LinkedIn, and here I am, choking on my own breath in a room full of people. I feel so utterly cut off from everyone, like there's an invisible glass wall between me and the rest of the batch.

Every evening, my hostel corridor gets so loud with guys planning their weekend trips and talking about their CGPAs. I literally wait inside my room with the lights off, listening through the door, just so I can walk to the washroom without bumping into anyone and having to make awkward small talk. I desperately want to make friends, but whenever someone says a simple 'hi' in the lobby, my throat tightens, I mutter something incoherent, and I walk away fast. They probably think I'm some arrogant snob, but in reality, I'm just incredibly lonely and terrified of messing up the only interaction I might get.

I forced myself to go to the coding club orientation today because my parents keep saying I need to build a 'network' to get a good package. The auditorium was packed, and the seniors were so confident, throwing out jokes and picking people from the crowd to speak. I was sitting near the back, literally praying they wouldn't look at me, with cold sweat running down my back. I couldn't take the noise and the social pressure anymore, so I slipped out the back door halfway through and sat in the empty library staircase crying. I feel like such a failure, I can't even handle a basic college club meet without losing my mind.

My roommate's birthday was last night, and they had this huge cake-smashing thing in the hostel wing with like thirty guys crammed into our room. I sat on my lower bunk, pretending to be deeply engrossed in my notes for the upcoming midterms, feeling completely invisible while everyone laughed and took videos for their Instagram stories. Someone finally asked me why I was being such a buzzkill and not joining in, and I just froze, unable to explain that the noise and the crowd were making my chest collapse. I ended up leaving the room to sleep in the common library, feeling like an absolute alien who doesn't belong anywhere on this campus.

It’s DBMS group project formation week and my hands literally started shaking when the prof said 'find your own teams of four.' Everyone immediately stood up, high-fiving, grabbing seats next to each other, and I just froze, staring at my VS Code screen pretending I was debugging some deep error. I ended up being the leftover person the prof had to manually assign to a random group, and I heard one of them sigh. I’ve been hiding in my hostel room since 4 PM, skipping dinner because the thought of walking into that mess hall and seeing them all sit together makes me want to throw up.

Every Friday night is the same torture. I hear the guys down the corridor laughing, blasting music, and planning their weekend ride to the highway dhaba, while I’m sitting here staring at my half-finished Compiler Design assignment. I walked past their open door to go to the washroom, and my chest got so tight I couldn't even look them in the eye or say a simple 'hi'—I just stared at the floor like a freak. I want to be part of them so badly, but my throat completely locks up and I convince myself they’d just find me incredibly boring anyway.

I tried to attend the coding club's orientation today because I promised myself I’d make at least one friend this semester. But the moment I reached the seminar hall door and saw fifty people talking in tight little circles, my heart started hammering against my ribs and I couldn't breathe. I spun around, ran down the stairs, and locked myself in a stall in the library washroom, crying silently so nobody would hear me. My CGPA is 9.2 but I can't even open a door to meet people; how am I ever going to clear a placement interview if I'm this pathetic?

I dread lunch more than my end-sem backlogs. Today I finally sat down at an empty table in the mess, but then a group of seniors and classmates sat near me and started discussing their summer internships. I wanted to add something, to just say 'hey, that's awesome,' but my mind went totally blank and I literally forgot how to swallow my food naturally. I felt like they were all judging the awkward way I was holding my spoon, so I cleared my half-eaten plate and practically fled. I’m starving in my room right now, surviving on raw Maggi noodles because I'm too terrified of being perceived.

My batchmates made a separate WhatsApp group for the weekend trip to the hills, and I only found out because one of them accidentally opened his gallery next to me during the DSA lab. I saw the photos—everyone was smiling, bonfire, hoodies, looking so close and comfortable. I went back to my PG, turned off my phone, and lay in the dark for hours feeling this massive, hollow ache in my chest. I don't know what is wrong with me, why I can never just easily slide into conversations like they do without my stomach twisting into painful knots.

Every time I walk into the DSA coding lab, my chest gets so tight I can barely breathe. Everyone already has their lab partners, and I’m just standing there holding my laptop like an idiot. The professor asked who didn't have a group, and I couldn't even raise my hand because I was terrified of everyone turning around to look at me. I ended up sitting in the last row alone, pretending to debug a code that doesn't even exist, feeling like a complete ghost while everyone else is laughing and collaborating.

I spent the entire weekend staring at my hostel room wall because the thought of going to the mess hall for dinner makes me physically sick. I can hear the loud laughter of the regional language groups from the corridor, and I just know if I walk in there alone, I'll freeze up trying to find a seat. I’m living on packets of raw Maggi and water just to avoid the humiliation of sitting by myself at a table for four. I feel so pathetic, like I'm wasting my college years while everyone else is building memories.

There's an orientation event for the tech club tonight, and I've changed my shirt three times already because my sweat is showing through. I want to go so bad because my CGPA is slipping and I need to build projects, but my hands are shaking just looking at the RSVP email. I know if I go, I'll just stand in the corner, scroll my phone pretending to be busy, and leave early feeling even more isolated than before. It feels like there is this thick glass wall between me and the rest of the world, and I don't have the script to talk to anyone.

My parents keep sending me links to WhatsApp groups of relatives whose kids got high placement packages, asking me why I haven't joined any college societies yet. I can't explain to them that I skip the corridor walks during break because my heart races if a classmate makes eye contact. I'm so scared of being asked 'what are your plans' or 'which domain are you working in' that I've started taking the stairs to the sixth floor just to avoid the elevator conversations. I am completely drowning in this campus, and I feel so invisible yet so exposed.

It’s my hostel room partner's birthday today, and they are planning a cake-cutting in our room at midnight with twenty other guys. I am literally hiding in the library toilet right now, hoping they finish before I have to go back. I feel like such a freak because I can't even handle a simple celebration without feeling like I'm going to throw up from the sheer social pressure. If I go back, I'll have to make small talk, and if I stay here, I'm the weird roommate who ruined the vibe.
